candidates.evidence: Two sharp first-order lines at 360.3 (E2g/E' in-plane) and 420.3 cm-1 (A1g/A1' out-of-plane), matching WS2 (bulk ~356/421 cm-1; monolayer ~357/418-419 cm-1 at 532 nm). No other TMD fits: MoS2 is 383/408, WSe2 ~250, MoSe2 ~241/286, and none of those have lines here. No peaks between 450 and 1100 cm-1, so no substrate or other-phase lines.

hint_reasoning: The spectrum is consistent with WS2. The only two sample lines, at 360.3 and 420.3 cm-1, fall where the WS2 in-plane E2g (~356-358) and out-of-plane A1g (~418-421) modes are reported at 532 nm (Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013); Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013)). The 60 cm-1 splitting is below the bulk value (~65) and close to the monolayer/few-layer value (~61-62). No other common TMD has modes at these positions. Three things are unusual: (1) the E2g is ~3-4 cm-1 above typical WS2 values, (2) the 2LA(M) band at ~350 cm-1 is absent or very weak although it is usually strong under 532 nm resonance, and (3) the A1g/E2g intensity ratio is low (~0.18). These do not contradict WS2, but they limit how precisely layer number and strain can be stated.

peaks.source: Lorentzian fit with a quadratic background over 300-470 cm-1. Mode assignment from Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013).

properties.name: E2g-A1g separation
properties.value: 60.0 cm-1, which is less than the bulk value (~65 cm-1) and close to the monolayer/few-layer value (~61-62 cm-1). This suggests a thin flake, but strain or doping can shift the modes, so it is not a unique layer count.
properties.source: Measured peak positions compared with Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013).

properties.name: E2g position
properties.value: 360.3 cm-1, about 3-4 cm-1 above typical WS2 values (356-358 cm-1). Possible causes are compressive strain, doping or a calibration offset.

properties.name: A1g/E2g intensity ratio
properties.value: about 0.18 from Lorentzian amplitudes (A1g ~3460 vs E2g ~19600 counts), compared with a typical ~0.3-0.5 for monolayer WS2

limits: The two lines at 360/420 cm-1 point to WS2, but the data cannot give a definite layer number: the 60 cm-1 splitting is only suggestive, and strain or doping can shift it.
The E2g position (360.3 cm-1) is higher than typical, and the data cannot separate strain, doping and calibration effects.

2LA(M) near 350 cm-1 and LA(M) near 176 cm-1 are not resolved. A weak 2LA(M) shoulder cannot be fully excluded because it overlaps the strong E2g line, and the weak component a fit placed near 334 cm-1 is not statistically meaningful.
Only unpolarized single-spectrum data are available, so mode symmetry (E2g vs A1g) is assigned from position only, not from polarization.
The 162.56 cm-1 feature is a single-point spike. It is treated as a cosmic ray and not as a low-frequency mode.
The substrate is not specified, and no Si line at 520.7 cm-1 is seen (the data are flat there, ~6700-6800 counts).
The measurement does not rule out a trace of WO3 or oxidation, because no features are resolved above the noise.
